leads.title: Penal Code of 1791 and Penal Code of 1810
leads.documents: Decriminalization of same-sex sexual activity in private in France; policy retained in Code followed in nations and French colonies that adopted it - legal basis for Saint Barthelemy
leads.detail: No URL in excerpt; cited as 'Penal Code of 1791 made no mention of same-sex relations in private' retained in 'Penal Code of 1810'

leads.title: Law opening marriage to same-sex couples 2013 - Journal Officiel
leads.documents: Legalizes same-sex marriage throughout France; article states same-sex marriage is legal in all overseas departments and territories including Saint Barthelemy
leads.detail: No URL in excerpt; cited as National Assembly vote 329-229, Senate approval 12 April, Constitutional Council ruled constitutional 17 May 2013, signed 18 May 2013, published in Journal Officiel next day, first ceremony 29 May Montpellier

leads.title: French Penal Code Article 225-1 as amended 18 November 2016
leads.documents: Prohibits discrimination on grounds of sexual orientation and gender identity - employment, housing, services protections applicable to Saint Barthelemy
leads.detail: No URL in excerpt; cited as 1985 law for sexual orientation, July 2012 added 'sexual identity', 18 November 2016 law replaced with 'gender identity'

leads.title: French Labour Code Chapter 2 - Code du travail
leads.documents: Prohibits exclusion from recruitment, sanction, dismissal or discriminatory measure on account of sexual orientation, gender identity, morals, gender among others
leads.detail: No URL in excerpt; quoted verbatim in article starting 'No person may be excluded from a recruitment process...'

leads.title: Law of 31 December 2004 / Law on Freedom of the Press of 29 July 1881 Title 3 Articles 20-21
leads.documents: Creates hate-speech and hate-crime machinery: makes homophobic comments illegal, increases penalties when assault/murder motivated by sexual orientation; created Haute autorite de lutte contre les discriminations et pour l'egalite
leads.detail: No URL in excerpt; cited as National Assembly approved amendment 31 Dec 2004, max penalty 45000 euro and/or 12 months, amends 1881 Press Law for injury, defamation, incitement to hatred

leads.title: European Court of Human Rights B. vs France (1992)
leads.documents: Court ruling that changed French ban on legal gender change; required France to allow legal gender change even after medical/surgical transition
leads.detail: No URL in excerpt; cited as '1992 case, B. vs France at the European Court of Human Rights changed this'

leads.title: Law of 18 November 2016 on legal gender change - effective 1 January 2017
leads.documents: Allows transgender people to legally change gender without sex reassignment surgery, sterilisation, psychiatrist certificates; requires court application; first-name change by registry office
leads.detail: No URL in excerpt; cited as Senate approved 6 Nov 2015, National Assembly 24 May 2016 and 12 July 2016 and 12 Oct, Constitutional Council ruled constitutional 17 Nov, signed 18 Nov 2016, published Journal Officiel next day

leads.title: ILGA-Europe 2022 report on gender affirming healthcare in France
leads.documents: Institutional human-rights report documenting lack of self-determination, extended waiting times, inequitable access by location; recommended informed consent and self-determination
leads.detail: No URL in excerpt; cited as 'report published in 2022 by ILGA-Europe found significant issues with the provision of gender affirming healthcare in France'

leads.title: DILCRAH - French Interministerial Delegation for the Fight Against Racism, Anti-Semitism, and Anti-LGBT Hatred
leads.documents: Government rights machinery responsible for anti-LGBT hatred policy; article notes 2022 controversy over scientific committee president membership in The Little Mermaid Observatory
leads.detail: No URL in excerpt; cited as 'DILCRAH' with scientific committee controversy and resignation

leads.title: Overseas deputies vote record and 2014 overseas attitudes study
leads.documents: Documents enforcement climate for Saint Barthelemy: 1 deputy from Saint Martin and Saint Barthelemy voted against same-sex marriage; 2014 study 20% overseas saw homosexuality as sexuality like any other vs 77% metropolitan; first same-sex marriages in Saint Martin caused demonstrations
leads.detail: No URL in excerpt; cited in 'Overseas departments and territories' section: 27 overseas deputies breakdown 11 for, 11 against, 1 abstained; Saint Barthelemy noted as more open due to international celebrity tourism
